newsitem.title: MEXICO: North Mexico builders, gov't to launch houses plan.
newsitem.headline: North Mexico builders, gov't to launch houses plan.

text.p: The construction industry and a government housing agency will jointly launch an emergency program to build 3,000 homes in the northern Mexican state of Nuevo Leon, an industry leader said.

"We're putting up 3,000 homes...we'll supply the land and the urbanization program financed at eight to 10 years, and (government housing agency) Infonavit will supply the house, or about 70 percent," Hector Velasco, president of the Nuevo Leon branch of the National Construction Industry Chamber (CNIC), said in an interview Saturday.
"We think we can recover some 15,000 jobs in a year with this plan," Velasco said. "We should be launching it before October; Infonavit are looking on it favorably."
Velasco said that 10,000 homes were currently being built per year in Nuevo Leon, but 40,000 a year were needed.
"We should seek to create 50,000 jobs. We've lost 35,000. The building industry employs 57,000, 20,000 of whom are permanent and the rest casual," Velasco said.
The Nuevo Leon construction industry had slowed down to "a little below" 50 percent working capacity, he added, as spending on a poverty relief program in the state had ended.
"Activity has fallen off, as poverty relief funds for townships from the Social Development Ministry (Sedesol) have already been spent," Velasco said.

Sedesol had earmarked funds for basic infrastructure programs, such as drainage and paving for poor townships. These programs had provided work for 6,000 to 8,000 people, but those jobs were now likely to come to an end.
The CNIC was thus seeking to have more such funds assigned to it, Velasco said, stressing it had previously fulfilled contract specifications on time.
"We need these funds to keep 6,000-8,000 people in work," Velasco said.
